result.summary: Extracts discrete helper methods from PeerManagerImpl::SendMessages() in src/net_processing.cpp, shrinking the main message dispatch loop from roughly 500 lines to under 90 lines. Seventeen move-only commits isolate message generation and timeout checks—including block announcements, getdata queueing, stall detection, and transaction trickling—followed by a cleanup commit that standardizes naming and conditionals.
result.problem: SendMessages() is a monolithic function handling all P2P message dispatching and timeout logic inline, interleaving distinct mutex scopes and relay flows. This makes navigation, lock analysis, and targeted review difficult for developers working on P2P message processing.
evidence: The author noted identifying this issue while reviewing net refactor #34824, citing that the 500-line inline implementation makes SendMessages() 'hard to navigate and review'.
Follows previous extraction patterns (#35502, #35148, #34059) and addresses a long-standing refactoring goal dating back to #9579 ('Make SendMessages easier to review').
result.scope_notes: Comprises 17 move-only commits meant to be reviewed with git --color-moved, followed by one commit that cleans up naming, whitespace, and minor conditional logic.
result.changed_since_previous: Incorporated upstream ping timeout handling into the extracted timeout helpers and added an 18th commit that cleans up naming (renaming MaybeSendInitialGetheaders to MaybeSendInitialGetHeaders), pointer formatting, and redundant boolean checks.
result.card: This PR extracts 17 move-only helper functions from PeerManagerImpl::SendMessages in src/net_processing.cpp, shrinking the main dispatch function from roughly 500 lines to under 90 lines. It addresses maintainability and review difficulty in the P2P message sending loop, fulfilling a refactoring goal dating back to #9579 and resurfaced during review of #34824. The PR introduces no intentional behavioral changes beyond changing the __func__ name in four debug log messages. No dependencies are declared.

risk.why: A mistake in lock acquisition scope or control flow across extracted helpers could stall block/tx downloads or prematurely disconnect peers.
